## Brief overview
The manuscript reports a randomised test of a brief mindfulness app for student wellbeing. The core contribution rests on a between-group effect that is currently undermined by an impossible descriptive statistic (REV-STAT-0001, REV-CON-0001).

## Developmental feedback
The central concern is the reported programme-group mean of 8.40 on a 1 to 7 scale (REV-STAT-0001). Because the consistency screen records the same value as an impossible result (REV-CON-0001), the effect estimate cannot be trusted until the descriptives are recomputed. The significance claim is reported without its test statistic (REV-STAT-0002), and one load-bearing reference could not be located (REV-REF-0001). The effect also sits above the internal benchmark (REV-CTX-0001), and swarm review found the practical framing fragile (REV-SWM-0001). Structurally, the reporting standard is CONSORT and the participant flow diagram is missing (REV-MAP-0001).

## What would change my recommendation
Recomputing the descriptives from raw data and reconciling REV-STAT-0001 and REV-CON-0001 would move this from major revision toward minor revision.

selfCritique.strongestObjection: The provisional rubric leans on the statistical bottleneck; if REV-STAT-0001 is later reconciled, several scores would rise and the narrative emphasis would shift.
confidenceRaisers: The corrected descriptive statistics, which would confirm or retire the central concern before the scores settle.
